problem: Vision-based navigation policies trained on public datasets are tied to the robot, camera and dynamics that collected the data, so they do not transfer to new robots with different size, turning radius, or camera placement/intrinsics.
motivation: Robot datasets are heterogeneous and collecting new data per platform is costly. If scene geometry can be recovered from monocular images, the same data can be re-rendered and relabeled for counterfactual robots, giving effectively unlimited augmented experience.
key_idea: Recover a point cloud from monocular images via self-supervised depth, then synthesize novel-camera views and train a robot-size/velocity-conditioned policy with a geometry-aware collision loss on the point cloud, so one policy serves many robots.
insight: Augmenting at the trajectory level (both observations and action supervision) lets one policy generalize across cameras and robot parameters. Ablations in Table I[a] show that removing view augmentation (PGA 0.801 vs 0.833) or the geometric loss (PCF 0.919 vs 0.945) each hurts, and Table I[c] shows using all three datasets gives the best offline loss. Viewpoint-change experiments (Table II) show ExAug does not degrade across a 30 cm camera-height change, while DVMPC does.
method: Depth/point cloud recovery: self-supervised monocular depth and pose estimation (Zhou/Godard/Depth360 style with a learnable camera model) trained on the mixed datasets, back-projecting depth into a 3D point cloud.

Novel view synthesis: transform the point cloud to a target camera pose and intrinsics, then project with 3D warping, four-neighbor splatting ordered by depth, and weighted bilinear interpolation to synthesize target-camera images (128x128).

Robot-conditioned policy: an 8-layer CNN encodes current and goal images. FC layers output Ns velocity/angular-velocity commands conditioned on robot radius rs and velocity limits (scaled tanh), plus traversability estimates from an FC head.

Geometry-aware objective: J = Jpose + wg*Jgeo + wd*Jdiff + wt*Jtrav. Jgeo penalizes point-cloud points falling inside a cylindrical robot body (random radius in [0,1] m, height 0.45 m) along the integrated trajectory, with density-normalizing weights. The others are pose regression, velocity smoothness, and traversability regression.

Training data mix: GO Stanford (indoor TurtleBot2, spherical camera), RECON (off-road Jackal, fisheye) and KITTI (on-road driving). A separate policy is trained per target camera, and the goal is sampled within Np steps of the current frame.

Navigation system: topological graph localization (nearest node among 5 adjacent subgoals) feeds the policy. Receding-horizon control uses only the first command, and a safety module pivot-turns when predicted traversability p1 < 0.5. A separate rs' for collision prediction is allowed at inference.

setting.backbone: 8-layer CNN + FC heads (trained from scratch) plus a self-supervised depth/pose network
setting.training_data: Three public datasets: GO Stanford (10 h), RECON (30 h), and 10 KITTI Odometry sequences, augmented with synthetic novel-camera views and counterfactual robot-size/velocity labels
setting.observation: Monocular RGB image (current and subgoal), from spherical, wide-FoV fisheye, or narrow-FoV RealSense cameras
setting.action_space: Continuous linear/angular velocity commands (predicted horizon of Ns steps, first step executed)
setting.privileged: none (a topological map of subgoal images is built by prior teleoperation; the target camera's intrinsics/extrinsics are assumed known)

results: With the same spherical camera, ExAug more than doubles DVMPC's goal-arrival rate indoors (0.889 vs 0.389) and reduces collisions by about 75%. It also outperforms DVMPC even with a narrow-FoV RealSense camera (indoor GA 0.500 vs 0.389). It stays robust when the camera height changes (TC 0.939 at low height vs DVMPC 0.678) and transfers to a new LoCoBot.
limitations: Robot parameters (size, velocity limits) must be chosen manually for conditioning, and a separate policy is trained per target camera.
Robots must be structurally similar (e.g. forward-facing cameras), and synthesized views are blurry/noisy and depend on monocular depth quality.
Evaluation is small-scale (12 environments x 3 trials) and compares against few baselines.
builds_on: Probabilistic visual navigation with bidirectional image prediction
